sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:192795
Court No. - 66
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 38254 of 2024

Applicant :- Johara
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Kameshwar Singh,Sudhanshu Kumar Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Raj Kumar Prajapati
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Rejoinder affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Kameshwar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Raj Kumar Prajapati, learned counsel for the informant and Dr. S.B. Maurya, learned AGA-I for the State.
3.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 62 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Girwan,
District Banda during pendency of the trial.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture, she has been made accused in the present matter along with her other family members including husband of the deceased.
5.

He further submits that deceased died almost after six years of her marriage and this fact itself suggests that FIR of the present case is based on false and frivolous facts as it is hard to believe that Johara vs State Of U.P. on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56369130/
1
even after six years of marriage deceased was subjected to cruelty for demand of dowry.

6. He further submits, actually some dispute arose between husband and wife due to the reason that husband wanted to go outside the native place and deceased insisted to accompany him and after this dispute she hanged herself and only being mother-in-law of the deceased, applicant has been made accused in the present matter.
He further submits, post mortem report also suggests that deceased died due to hanging.

7. He further submits, however, earlier also deceased lodged a FIR under Section 498A IPC against her husband, applicant and other family members but it appears that due to the matrimonial dispute deceased lodged that FIR and in that FIR also only being mother-in-law, applicant has been made accused.
It is next submitted, subsequently dispute was settled and deceased started living in her matrimonial home.

8. He further submits, immediately after the incident, husband of the applicant i.e. father-in-law of the deceased, informed the police and on his information Panchayatnama was conducted on 01.03.2024 and in the Panchayatnama father-in-law of the deceased was one of the witness along with family members of the deceased and at that time no objection was raised by the family members of the deceased but on the next day FIR was lodged.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits, inquest report of the deceased has been annexed at page-41 of the paper-book.
9.
He further submits that applicant is a lady and there is no specific allegation against her and in the present matter she is in jail since 02.07.2024.

10. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased and her daughter-in-law died within seven years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry and earlier also deceased herself lodged a FIR under Section 498A IPC against her husband and other family members including applicant but they could not dispute the fact that there is no specific allegation against the applicant and even in the earlier case lodged by the deceased under Section 498A IPC there was no specific allegation against the applicant.
11.

They further could not dispute the fact that information of the death of the deceased was given by her father-in-law i.e. husband of the applicant to the police and on his information inquest was conducted and in the inquest even family members of the deceased were the inquest witnesses but in spite of that FIR of the present case was lodged next day.
They further could not dispute the fact that post mortem report suggests that deceased died due to hanging.
12. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

13. However, daughter-in-law of the applicant died within seven years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home and there is also allegation of demand of dowry and it also reflects that deceased earlier also in the month of August, 2022 lodged a FIR under Section 498A IPC against her husband and her family members including applicant but from the Johara vs State Of U.P. on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56369130/
2 post mortem it reflects, deceased died due to hanging, therefore, prima facie, it appears to be a case of suicidal death.

14. Further, after the alleged suicide committed by the deceased her father-in-law informed the police and on his information inquest was conducted and at the time of inquest family members of the deceased were not only present but they were also inquest witnesses but in spite of that FIR of the present case was lodged next day.

15. Further, from the FIR under Section 498A IPC, earlier lodged by the deceased, which has been annexed along with rejoinder affidavit filed by the applicant, it reflects that on the basis of general allegation applicant has been made accused in that case too along with husband of the deceased and it also reflects that in that case matter was settled and thereafter deceased started living in her matrimonial home.
16. Further, applicant is a lady and there is no specific allegation against her and in the present matter she is in jail since 02.07.2024.

17. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
18. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

19. Let the applicant - Johara be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
20. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

21. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 9.12.2024 AK Pandey  Johara vs State Of U.P. on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56369130/
